lines:
The machine-local persistence boundary contains canonical semantic Chat/Run events and operational indexes in SQLite, schema-versioned JSON configuration and workflows, ordinary artifact files, extension inventory, recurring-error evidence, bounded debug capture, rotating diagnostics, and the noncanonical runtime journal required to resume active portable Chats on the same machine.

Only the trusted core commits canonical history. Transactions preserve ordered event identity, attempt identity, checkpoints, and outbox-style delivery metadata. Secrets are excluded and referenced by opaque credential-store handles. Streaming fragments are not canonical unless detailed capture is explicitly enabled. Local history is canonical only for Chats not configured for portable storage.

For a Chat whose semantic history is canonical in the Portable Session Repository, this boundary may store only machine-local operational facts keyed to the portable CommitId/head hash: the full locally bound frozen snapshot reference, pending command/invocation deduplication, dispatch and worker-control outbox state, process generations, queued-input delivery cursor, pending approval state, and recovery reconciliation facts. Those rows are not a semantic event stream, cannot be exported as authority, and expire or become inert when their binding no longer matches the verified portable head.

Incremental runtime reads (2026-09-17): Provide sequence-fenced tail reads, indexed event-kind and record identity queries, and scalar stream-head access. Runtime append and lookup must not decode an entire operational stream merely to find its head or one invocation. Canonical evidence remains immutable and durable-before-dispatch; disposable caches advance only after successful commits and reconcile external appends without replaying tools. Specification: docs/context-continuation-performance.md.
